analysis.title: Retail Radar - Sep 30 – Weak Sentiment, Record Tilt to TLT
key_insights: Retail flows stayed subdued at the 12th percentile for the week. September was the weakest month for retail activity since Dec 2024. Daily flows held in the 15-30th percentile range regardless of price action.

ETF flows probed new lows (3rd percentile) while single stock flows edged down to the 35th percentile. September monthly ETF flows approached levels last seen during the 2025 Momentum Unwind, which preceded the Liberation Day buy-the-dip episode.

Weekly ETF weakness came from International, Crypto and Commodity ETF flows. Fixed income ETF inflows picked up, led by the largest rotation into long-end Treasury ETFs on record (+5.4z), driven mainly by TLT (6.1z) as yields kept drifting higher.

Mag 7 continued to dominate single-stock purchases. Outside Tech, every sector was net sold when Mag 7 names are excluded. Retail favored Semis and Hardware over Software, with NVDA driving Semis purchases.

Retail made no discernible incremental move to position ahead of Micron's earnings (0.0z). Micron reported a revenue and earnings beat with guidance above expectations, and the stock rose about 2% after hours.

Small caps kept underperforming large caps as Treasury yields tested new 22-year highs. Smaller companies rely more on short-term floating-rate bank financing, generally under 5-year maturities. Retail is typically a net buyer of Russell 1000 stocks and a net seller of Russell 2000 stocks, a trend accelerating since March.

Median short interest as a % of shares outstanding is at the 99.8th percentile for Russell 2000 companies and the 96.2th percentile for the S&P 500. The July Momentum Unwind drawdown pushed S&P 500 short interest to comparatively lower levels.

Energy retail flows flipped from mildly positive or flat to mildly negative as flows through the Saudi East-West pipeline were restored. Oil held near $100 even though Middle East oil exports are 11% below pre-war levels. Crude flows are at 98% of pre-war levels while product exports are at 58%, and Hormuz flows have nearly returned to late June highs.

Retail flows were $4.1B this week against a 12-month average of $6.8B/week. ETFs took +$3.4B and single stocks $0.7B. Broad-based large cap equity ETFs took +$1.4B, long-term Treasury funds +$260M and equity style call/put writing +$188M.
Mag 7 retail activity: bought NVDA (+$1,286M), TSLA (+$514M), GOOG/L (+$153M) and AMZN (+$146M). Sold AAPL (-$18M), MSFT (-$27M) and META (-$48M).
Outside Mag 7, retail favored Tech (+$194M) and was a net seller of all other sectors, led by Financials (-$278M), Communications (-$276M) and Materials (-$199M).
Top retail stocks: NVDA, TSLA, SNDK (+$327M), GOOG/L, AMZN. Bottom five: INTC (-$199M), SPCX (-$171M), ORCL (-$88M), NBIS (-$60M), BE (-$54M).
Retail options share is off its highs, with the rolling 1-month average at the 93.5th percentile. Most traded options names: TSLA, META, MU, NVDA, AMD, SNDK, AMZN, MSFT, GOOG/L, AAPL.
Non-retail futures traders bought $33B last week, led by ES ($19.7B), NQ (~$12.8B) and RTY (~$0.5B).

CCL rose 13% after a strong quarter despite rising oil prices and a raised full-year guide. Retail sold CCL ($14.4M on 9/29, -3.5z). RCL and NCLH rose 5-6%. JPM derivatives analysts have a CCL trade recommendation.
Everpure (P) reported an earnings beat and above-consensus guidance for F3Q27 and FY27. The stock is up 18% since 9/23 and was recently added to the S&P 500. Retail sold $12M last week (-1.2z).

MGM is reportedly considering a bid for PPLI (WSJ). JPM analysts say it would work like an accelerated buyback for 27% of MGM stock, since PPLI owns 66.8M MGM shares. MGM is down about 10% since the news and PPLI is up 15%.
Meme-stock squeeze risk is decreasing as retail sells high short-interest names. Short interest in TLT is 19.4% of float with a retail imbalance of +4.7z on 9/29.
Average stock idiosyncratic risk (residual of market, sector, macro and style factors) is at the 92nd percentile in both the Russell 2000 and S&P 500.

market_movers.rationale: MGM is rated OW at $31.05. JPM analysts say a PPLI bid could work like an accelerated buyback for 27% of MGM's stock.
PPLI is rated OW at $41.96. It owns 66.8M MGM shares, and a deal could limit the tax liability on that stake (est. cost basis ~$19/sh vs ~$34/sh MGM price).
Micron reported a revenue and EPS beat with above-consensus guidance, and the stock rose about 2% after hours. Retail did not position ahead of the print.
Shares rose 13% on a strong quarter and a raised full-year guide despite higher oil prices. Retail sold into the move.
Beat with above-consensus F3Q27 and FY27 guidance, helped by resilient demand after price increases and better component supply. Hyperscaler shipments are expected to reach tens of EBs in FY28.
Shares rose 7% in the past week after a large biopharma company chose Veeva's Vault CRM, bringing global commitments to 14 of the top 20 biopharma companies.
Shares rose over 170% after two experimental eye drugs met their primary endpoints in a Phase 3 study.

sector_views.rationale: Retail was a net buyer of Tech (+$194M) while selling every other sector outside Mag 7. Semis and Hardware were favored over Software.
Retail was the largest net seller of Financials (-$278M) among sectors outside Mag 7. This is a flow observation, not a JPM rating.
Retail flows turned mildly negative as Saudi East-West pipeline flows were restored.

earnings_insights: Micron (MU) reported 9/30 after the close: revenue and EPS beat as largely expected, and next-quarter guidance above expectations. The stock rose about 2% after hours. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.
Carnival (CCL) reported a very strong quarter despite rising oil prices and raised full-year guidance. Shares rose 13%. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.

Everpure (P) reported an earnings beat and above-expectation guidance for F3Q27 (Oct-end) and FY27 (Jan-end). Drivers: demand held up better than feared after industry-wide price increases, and supply confidence improved. The stock is up 18% since 9/23.
Veeva (VEEV) disclosed a large biopharma company chose its Vault CRM. The announcement was consistent with guidance but landed faster than the Street expected.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Oil held near $100 even though Middle East exports are 11% below pre-war levels.
Crude flows have nearly fully recovered. Product exports are at 58%.
Higher yields weigh on small caps, which depend on short-term floating-rate bank financing.

crypto_views: Crypto ETF flows were among the weaker retail ETF categories this week.
Crypto-linked names CIFR, WULF and HUT rank among the most discussed on social media, with retail net sellers of CIFR (-1.2z) and WULF (-2.2z) and a small buyer of HUT (+0.7z).
risk_factors: Rising Treasury yields at 22-year highs pressure small caps through floating-rate financing costs.
Weak retail participation, with September the weakest month since Dec 2024.
Oil near $100 with product exports still at 58% of pre-war levels.
Record Russell 2000 short interest alongside elevated idiosyncratic risk (92nd percentile).
